{{WTA Tour sidebar}}

The '''WTA Tier I tournaments'''<ref>{{cite web|last=Tandon|first=Kamakashi|title=Ten notable features of the Roadmap|url=https://www.espn.com/sports/tennis/columns/story?columnist=kamakshi_tandon&id=3670301|work=29 October 2008|date=29 October 2008 |publisher=ESPN|access-date=20 May 2014}}</ref> were [[Women's Tennis Association]] [[tennis]] elite tournaments held from 1990 until the end of the 2008 season. From 1988 to 1990, the different levels of WTA tournaments were referred to by the term 'Category', and there were 5 categories.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Barrett|first1=John|title=World of Tennis 1990|date=1990|publisher=Collins Willow|location=London|isbn=0002183552|page=163}}</ref> Two of the Tier I tournaments, [[Indian Wells Masters|Indian Wells]] and [[Miami Masters|Miami]], were also joint events held simultaneously with the [[Association of Tennis Professionals|ATP Tour]] [[ATP Masters Series|Masters Series]].

There were initially 6 Tier I tournaments held annually from 1990. The list expanded to 8 events in 1993, 9 in 1997 and 10 in 2004, before being scaled back to 9 for 2008.

In [[2009 WTA Tour|2009]] the WTA changed the tournament categories, so that the majority of Tier I and Tier II tournaments were in one category, [[WTA Premier Tournaments|Premier Tournaments]], split into three categories.

; '''Winners of 6 series tournaments on hard:'''
* {{flagicon|SUI}} Hingis (Tokyo 96, Miami 97, Indian Wells 98, Canada 99, Zurich 00, Moscow 00).

; '''Winners of 5 series tournaments on hard:'''
* {{flagicon|RUS}} Sharapova (Tokyo 05, Indian Wells 06, San Diego 06, Zurich 06, Doha 08).

; '''Winners of 3 series tournaments on clay:'''
* {{flagicon|ESP}} Martinez (Rome 93, Hilton Head 94, Berlin 98).
* {{flagicon|SUI}} Hingis (Hilton Head 97, Rome 98, Berlin 99).

; '''Winners of the series tournaments on three surfaces:'''
* {{flagicon|US}} Navratilova (Chicago 90, Hilton Head 90, Tokyo 93).

A number of players hold records for winning the tournaments multiple times, while other records are achieved for successive tournament wins, mini-combination victories amongst others.
* Conchita Martínez won the Italian Open four straight times, from 1993 to 1996, and reached the final in 1997.
* Martina Hingis has won all the different Tier I tournaments except for the San Diego event, which became a Tier I event in 2004, during her three-year withdrawal from the sport which ended in late 2005.
